messages:
maria: heads up — eu-west1 GPU pool is hitting a scheduling backlog right now. lots of pods Pending with PodFitsError and some immediate evictions as nodes drain. spotted after a maintenance window + spot reclaim overlapped :grimace: 

cheng: can you paste the `kubectl get pods` for the pending ones? curious if it's affinity/taints or just resource fragmentation

maria: here are a few events from the pending set:
```
Events:
  Normal   FailedScheduling  2m (x12 over 10m)  default-scheduler  0/48 nodes are available: 36 Insufficient memory, 12 node(s) had taint {gpu-maintenance: yes}, matched by tolerations, 20 node(s) had insufficient allocatable GPUs.
  Warning  Evicted           1m                 kubelet             Pod "train-job-42" was evicted: The node was marked for drain
```

alex: weird — allocatable GPUs low but capacity shows free GPUs on some nodes? maybe GPUs are fragmented across many nodes with strict anti-affinity rules causing binpack failure. also saw a burst of daemonset jobs pinned to a subset of nodes earlier.

jordana: ops-bot just posted a drain schedule for eu-west1-b at 2123456000, we had two overlap windows (b and c) starting ~2123455800 and 2123455900. that explains the simultaneous drains.

ops-bot: automated-notification: planned-drain eu-west1-b started by infra-team (job/maintenance-2026-03). Estimated 30m.

maria: scheduler-bot shows 64 pending GPU pods queued in the cluster-queue "gpu-queue". many have podAntiAffinity requiredDuringScheduling which prevents colocating on remaining nodes.

scheduler-bot: alert: 64 pending pods; top failure reasons: PodFitsError (anti-affinity: 39), InsufficientGPU (25), TaintTolerationMismatch (10).

cheng: quick mitigation idea: relax requiredDuringScheduling -> preferredDuringScheduling for the oldest 20 pending pods so they can land on nodes with existing GPUs. we can target pods with label `redwood/eviction-priority=high` first.

alex: +1. alternatively we can temporarily cordon fewer nodes (skip one of the drains) but that requires infra approval. changing affinity is lower blast radius.

jordana: I can approve a manual hold on the drain for eu-west1-c for 15m — that should give the scheduler time to backfill. but we still need a descheduler/defrag action to consolidate after drains finish.

maria: taking action: will patch kube-mutating job to convert required->preferred for top 25 pending pods with that label. command I'll run:
```bash
kubectl get pods -l redwood/pend=GPU -o name | head -n 25 | xargs -I{} kubectl patch {} --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/affinity/podAntiAffinity/requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution","value":null}]'
```

cheng: careful — that patch can blow up for pods that actually need isolation. limit to label `redwood/allow-soft-affinity=true`. and add a 10m TTL via annotation so we revert after the pressure subsides.

maria: updated plan: I'll target `redwood/allow-soft-affinity=true`, add annotation `redwood/temp-affinity-relax-until=2123457510` and only run for 15m.

scheduler-bot: action logged: temporary affinity relaxation applied to 18 pods by maria at 2123456200.

alex: while that's running, I'll trigger the defrag job (descheduler) with `--evict-unneeded=false --target-gpus=0.75` to try and coalesce smaller GPU allocations.

jordana: holding eu-west1-c drain for 15m now. infra team notified.

maria: after patch ~10 pods scheduled within 90s and started pulling images. still ~26 pending due to actual GPU scarcity on remaining nodes.

cheng: for medium term — we should add a backstop where the scheduler can prefer binpack scored by fractional GPU utilization rather than pure spreading for non-latency training jobs. file a tracking ticket?

alex: filing INFRA-2148: "adaptive binpacking heuristic for GPU workloads". I'll include replay of this thread + metrics.

jordana: postmortem note: overlap in maintenance windows triggered the cascade. ops runbook update: add a staggered drain guard and auto-hold if pending GPU pods > 15 for >5m.

maria: thanks all. follow-ups: alex owns ticket, jordana updates runbook, cheng will prototype scheduler score change. I'll monitor until drains finish and revert annotations at 2123457510. :thumbsup:
